items.title: Attrition release ‘Netherworld (The Final Collection)’
items.summary: English industrial band Attrition release 'Netherworld (The Final Collection)', a collection of unreleased recordings, out 6 November 2026 on Klanggalerie.
items.fullText:
English dark wave and industrial act Attrition released the compilation “Netherworld (The Final Collection)” on 6 November 2026 through Austria’s Klanggalerie label.

The album is available as a CD and as a digital download. The CD is a foldout digipack. The band’s own announcement describes the CD as a limited edition of 300; the release’s official Bandcamp page lists it as an edition of 55.

The twelve tracks were compiled from cassette mixes and DAT tapes and mastered by Martin Bowes at The Cage in Coventry, England, across 2025 and 2026. They include two songs recorded live in 1981, one recorded live in 1983, and a demo, alongside other previously unreleased material recorded on a Teac four-track portastudio. Some of the tracks later circulated on independent cassettes in the early 1980s or as digital downloads, without an official release until now.

Bowes plays synthesisers, drum programming and vocals on the album. Julia Waller contributes vocals and bass guitar, and Ashley Niblock plays synthesisers and keyboards. Robbo and Steve Hands each play drums on one track, and Pete Morris plays bass on “For Samantha.” The release is dedicated to Morris’s memory.

“Netherworld (The Final Collection)” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp and streaming on Spotify.

Tracklist for ‘Netherworld (The Final Collection)’

  1. The Hanged Man
  2. Tomb
  3. This Final Push
  4. Shadowdance
  5. I was so surprised
  6. Neuroses (Live 1981)
  7. Divisions (Live 1981)
  8. Mind Drop (Demo)
  9. The Wrecking Ground
  10. (My) Parade
  11. For Samantha
  12. Prayer for the Head (Live 1983)

About Attrition

Attrition is an English dark wave band formed in Coventry in 1980 by Martin Bowes and Julia Niblock, emerging from the city’s early-1980s post-punk scene. Chris Bowes, Martin’s brother, played guitar in the band’s earliest line-up before Julia’s brother Ashley Niblock joined on synthesiser. The band’s sound has since spanned dark wave, EBM, neoclassical dark wave, industrial and dark ambient.

Attrition’s debut album, “The Attrition of Reason,” appeared on Third Mind Records in autumn 1984, followed by “Smiling, at the Hypogonder Club” in 1985 and “In The Realm of the Hungry Ghosts,” the band’s last release on Third Mind. “At the Fiftieth Gate” followed in 1988 on Belgium’s Antler-Subway Records, and “A Tricky Business” in 1991 on Italy’s Contempo Records, with European editions through the German labels Hyperium and Trisol. A compilation on the US label Projekt introduced the band to American audiences, and 1996’s “3 Arms And A Dead Cert” became their first full release for Projekt. Attrition founded their own label, Two Gods, in 2006.

The band has continued to revisit its archive alongside new work: a live recording of its first American show, from 1996, was released in 2022, the same year as the compilation “A Great Desire (1986 – 2004)” on vinyl. “Live in the Cage. 07.02.23” followed as a live album in 2023. Attrition announced “The Black Maria” in March 2024, its first new studio album in eight years, and toured Australia and New Zealand that year. A 7CD boxset, “Resurgence,” followed in early 2025, alongside “A Permanent View? Black Maria Remixed,” a remix companion to “The Black Maria” released exclusively on Bandcamp. “Netherworld (The Final Collection)” extends that archival work with recordings dating back to the band’s earliest years.

items.title: Last Moon In Moscow release debut single ‘Falling Down’
items.summary: Italian post-punk project Last Moon In Moscow release debut single "Falling Down," out 8 November 2026 with an official video.
items.fullText:
Italian post-punk and new wave project Last Moon In Moscow released the debut single “Falling Down” on 8 November 2026, with an official video. Last Moon In Moscow is the first solo project of Andrea Sabatini, former guitarist and bassist of the Italian synthwave band ZeroCall, based in Perugia, Italy.

Sabatini wrote and composed “Falling Down” and played guitars, bass and synthesizers on the track. Federico Sereni played drums and Matteo Silvestri provided vocals. Andrea Possiedi, founder of ZeroCall, mixed the track, and Pau Pinto Garcia mastered it. The official video uses historical optical animations.

“Falling Down” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp.

Conceived as a solo project, Last Moon In Moscow develops through collaborations with other musicians and remains open to future contributions. A first full-length album is expected in 2027.

About Last Moon In Moscow

Last Moon In Moscow is the solo project of Andrea Sabatini, based in Perugia, Italy, launched in 2026 with the release of “Falling Down.” Sabatini previously played guitar and bass in the Italian synthwave band ZeroCall, whose founder Andrea Possiedi mixed Last Moon In Moscow’s debut single. Though conceived as a solo outlet for Sabatini’s songwriting, the project works through collaborations with other musicians, drawing on drummer Federico Sereni and vocalist Matteo Silvestri for “Falling Down,” and remains open to further contributions on future releases. A first full-length album is planned for 2027.

items.title: In Strict Confidence release ‘Heartbreaker’, second single from ‘The Final Kiss’
items.summary: German EBM act In Strict Confidence release "Heartbreaker," the second single from their album "The Final Kiss," out 20 November 2026 on Minuswelt.
items.fullText:
German EBM and electro-industrial act In Strict Confidence released the single “Heartbreaker” on 13 November 2026. The track is the second single from the band’s forthcoming album “The Final Kiss,” due 20 November 2026 through Minuswelt.

“Heartbreaker” is available digitally in three versions: the original, a remix by Eisfabrik, and a NuDisco mix. Bandcamp carries a fourth version, an extended mix, alongside the other three. An official music video accompanies the single.

“Heartbreaker” follows “Fever,” the album’s lead single, released on 16 October 2026 with remixes by Controlled Fusion and Ash Code. “The Final Kiss” also includes “Blasphemous Rumours,” the band’s cover of the Depeche Mode song released as its own single in February 2026. The album is In Strict Confidence’s first studio release since 2018’s “Hate2Love.”

“Heartbreaker” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and other streaming platforms.

‘The Final Kiss’ due 20 November

“The Final Kiss” is available for pre-order on CD, as a limited-edition clear, marbled vinyl LP with the exclusive bonus track “Digital Cage,” and digitally through the band’s official shop. Its tracklist also includes “Fallen Angel,” “The Ocean’s Roar,” “Fake Love Again,” “Watch Us Fall,” “Where Is Your God Now?,” “No Secret” and “Schattenmelodie.”

In Strict Confidence has upcoming shows confirmed in Austria, Germany and Spain into 2027, including dates in Vienna, Weissenhäuser Strand, Oberhausen and Benidorm.

About In Strict Confidence

In Strict Confidence formed in Germany in 1989 under the name Seal of Secrecy, renaming itself In Strict Confidence in 1992, when the group narrowed from a quartet to the duo of Dennis Ostermann and Jörg Schelte. Stefan Vesper, a member of the original line-up, left in 1992 and returned in 2001. Heidi Pulkkinen, credited as HayDee Sparks, joined on guitars in 2008, and Nina de Lianin joined on vocals and lyrics in 2009, alongside Ostermann and Schelte in the band’s current line-up.

The band marked the 25th anniversary of its 1998 album “Face the Fear” with a reissue in 2023 and released a 25-years edition of “Cryogenix” in 2021, alongside a 2CD and double-vinyl “Mechanical Symphony” collection in 2023. In February 2026, the band released a cover of Depeche Mode’s “Blasphemous Rumours”, later folded into “The Final Kiss.” “Heartbreaker” follows lead single “Fever” and the album announcement in October, ahead of the album’s release on 20 November 2026.

items.title: EGOamp release ‘Testament’ EP featuring Airman’s ‘2001’ remix
items.summary: German synthpop band EGOamp release the four-track EP "Testament" on 13 November 2026, featuring Airman's remix of their track "2001."
items.fullText:
German synthpop band EGOamp released the four-track EP “Testament” on 13 November 2026. The release includes “2001 (Airmans AF-Red Eye Remix),” a new version of the band’s track “2001” remixed and produced by Airman.

The remix revisits the shutdown of HAL 9000, the shipboard computer aboard the Discovery One in Stanley Kubrick’s 1968 film “2001: A Space Odyssey,” expanding the dialogue between HAL and the crew with additional lines written for the remix. Those lines raise the question of whether HAL 9000 could have feelings, and whether an AI capable of doubt or fear could still be switched off. Airman staged the remix as what he calls a musical short film, with a harder, more cinematic sound than the original. Its subtitle, “af-red eye,” refers to HAL 9000’s red camera eye, read here as fearful in the moments before its own shutdown.

The original “2001” comes from EGOamp’s earlier EP “Petit Cinéaste,” released on Bandcamp. “Testament” carries four tracks: “Testament,” “Testament (Extended Remix),” “2001 (Airmans AF-Red Eye Remix)” and “I’ll Fight The Silence.”

“Testament” is available as a digital EP on Bandcamp.

About EGOamp

EGOamp are a German synthpop band known for combining classic science-fiction motifs with contemporary electronic production, as heard across EPs including “Petit Cinéaste.” “Testament,” the band’s new four-track EP, pairs original material with “2001 (Airmans AF-Red Eye Remix),” a remix and production credit from fellow German artist Airman. The release extends the thread the band opened on “Petit Cinéaste” between retro-futurist science fiction and dark electronic sound.

items.title: Lakeside X release ‘Babylon Kids’ single produced by Christian Eigner
items.summary: Lakeside X release "Babylon Kids," the title track of their new album, produced by Depeche Mode drummer Christian Eigner, out 13 November 2026.
items.fullText:
Prague-based alternative band Lakeside X released the single “Babylon Kids” on 13 November 2026. The track is produced by Depeche Mode drummer Christian Eigner, who also co-wrote the song, and is the title track of the band’s forthcoming fifth studio album, due 27 November 2026.

Eigner has written numerous Depeche Mode songs in addition to his work behind the drum kit, and his track “Suffer Well” was nominated for a Grammy Award in the Best Dance Recording category. “Babylon Kids” is his first full production and songwriting credit with Lakeside X, following the band’s 2025 announcement that they were working together. The song draws on British alternative music and post-punk, built around a beat that combines programmed samples with Eigner’s drumming, and moves further from the synth-pop roots Lakeside X started from than any of the band’s other recent singles.

Frontman and longtime sole songwriter Janne Marvannen said of the collaboration: “We first met Christian Eigner when we played shows together in the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary. We soon realised that being an outstanding drummer is just one side of him, and that we also clicked as musicians and songwriters. The first thing we tried doing together was this very song. Under his influence, the original idea changed completely, and what emerged was a track that is a genuine artistic collaboration. It’s something I’d never experienced before. As a band, we’ve always wanted to keep pushing ourselves forward, and this is a huge step for us as well as for me as a songwriter.”

“Babylon Kids” is about the search for meaning in a world mediated by screens, where connection is replaced by algorithms and dreams are traded for empty promises. The accompanying video was filmed in Stockholm and directed by the band’s own drummer, Igor Dvorský, continuing the visual thread of the band’s other 2026 singles: “Factory Flowers,” “Absinthe Dream” (shot around Vancouver) and “Nightrider” (filmed in Los Angeles).

‘Babylon Kids’ album due 27 November, Prague Planetarium show in December

The new album “Babylon Kids,” the band’s fifth, is due on 27 November 2026. Alongside Eigner, the band again worked with German producer Daniel Myer (Haujobb, Architect, DSTR, Covenant), who also produced their previous album, “Love Disappears.” Mix is by Niko Stoessl, mastering by Moimir Papalescu, and the single’s artwork is by Adrian T. Bell.

Immediately after the album’s release, on 4 December 2026, Lakeside X will perform at the Prague Planetarium, which features a 22-metre hemispherical LED dome at 8K resolution. The show, in front of a strictly limited audience, sold out shortly after it was announced.

About Lakeside X

Lakeside X are a Prague-based alternative band with a career spanning more than two decades and four studio albums, blending synth-pop roots with modern electronic music and an alternative guitar sound, built around the voice of frontman and songwriter Janne Marvannen. The current line-up is Marvannen (vocals, songwriting), Robert Broj (keyboards), Igor Dvorský (drums) and Jakub Zachoval (guitar).

The band has appeared at Wave-Gotik-Treffen and NCN Leipzig in Germany, EXIT Festival in Serbia, and Rock for People in the Czech Republic, and opened for Depeche Mode in Prague’s Letňany district in 2023. Since reuniting in 2022 after an extended break, the band has toured extensively in Germany, Poland, Hungary, Ireland and the UK, including a run of German dates in 2027 supporting Zeromancer.

Work on the new album began alongside Christian Eigner in 2025, and its singles arrived through the year: “Factory Flowers” earlier in 2026, “Absinthe Dream” in May, and “Nightrider” in July, each produced with Daniel Myer. “Babylon Kids” closes out that run of singles as the title track of the album itself, ahead of the Prague Planetarium show in December.

items.title: Lucifers Bathroom releases ‘Cursed’, third single from ‘Red Wax’ EP
items.summary: Lucifers Bathroom releases "Cursed," the third single from the forthcoming EP "Red Wax," out 13 November 2026 on Bandcamp and Spotify.
items.fullText:
Lucifers Bathroom, the dark alternative solo project from Germany, released the single “Cursed” on 13 November 2026. “Cursed” is the third single from the project’s forthcoming debut EP “Red Wax,” following “Shadows” on 17 April 2026 and “The Sigil” on 15 June 2026. One more single from “Red Wax” is still to come.

The cover art for “Cursed” reworks Eugène Delacroix’s painting “The Barque of Dante,” showing lost souls clawing at a boat crossing hell, tinted red and overlaid with a sigil. The project describes the track as looking straight at that weight, as a cold observer aware that the souls in the water are a reflection of ourselves. The theme runs through the project’s broader outlook: that the darkness carried inside can become emotion, and that emotion can heal.

“Shadows” and “The Sigil” received coverage from ReGen Magazine and Side-Line, and reached more than 100 radio plays combined in the US and UK.

“Cursed” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and Spotify.

About Lucifers Bathroom

Lucifers Bathroom is a dark alternative solo project from Germany, launched in 2026. The music combines heavy electronic sound design, atmospheric textures and vocals, drawing on dark alternative, industrial and gothic influences. The artist behind the project has chosen to stay anonymous, with every track written, produced and performed by one person.

The project’s debut EP, “Red Wax,” has been rolled out single by single over the course of 2026: “Shadows” arrived on 17 April, followed by “The Sigil,” mixed by Matthew Pansi, on 15 June. “Cursed” is the third single, with one more still to follow before the EP itself is released.

items.title: Two weeks left to submit your material for the Side-Line powered EBM compilation ‘Electronic Bodies 2’
items.summary: Side-Line Magazine is accepting submissions for "Electronic Bodies 2," the follow-up to its EBM compilation series. Send one WAV track via WeTransfer.
items.fullText:
There are two weeks left to submit your material for the Side-Line powered “Electronic Bodies 2,” the second volume in its electronic body music compilation series. Bands and artists making EBM and related electro-industrial styles can send in one track for consideration. The compilation will be released as a digital download via Side-Line’s Bandcamp page and promoted through Side-Line and its network of music media and DJs.

Attention: AI-generated tracks are NOT allowed.

The call follows “Electronic Bodies – Session 1”, Side-Line’s first EBM compilation, which brought together established names and lesser-known acts, covering old-school EBM, electro-industrial and more contemporary EBM styles.

What Side-Line is looking for in ‘Electronic Bodies 2’

For this second installment, Side-Line is again looking for bands and artists making EBM, old-school industrial, electro-industrial and related electronic body music. Tracks built around pounding sequencers, aggressive basslines, mechanical rhythms or stripped-down electronic arrangements all fit the brief. New, unsigned and established acts are all welcome; selection is based on the music itself, not the size of an artist’s audience or the number of releases already out.

How to submit a track for ‘Electronic Bodies 2’

Side-Line has set a few rules for submitting material, to be followed closely:

  • Send one mastered track in WAV format, selecting the strongest material available.
  • Submit it via WeTransfer.com to info@side-line.com; audio files sent as direct email attachments will not be accepted.
  • Name the file using the format “Artist – Track Title.wav”.
  • Artists must not be affiliated with GEMA, SABAM or similar collecting societies, since their licensing requirements could interfere with the compilation’s release.
  • Artists selected for the compilation will be contacted to complete the necessary paperwork.
  • Sending a track does not automatically guarantee inclusion; Side-Line will make a selection based on musical direction and the overall balance of the compilation.
  • Submission deadline: November 30, 2026.

The artwork accompanying this announcement is provisional and does not represent the final cover of “Electronic Bodies 2.” Side-Line will reveal the official artwork at a later stage.

About the Electronic Bodies series

Side-Line launched the Electronic Bodies series in January 2023, calling for submissions toward an old-school EBM compilation after a reader poll pointed the project at the early-1980s EBM sound of Belgium and its Scandinavian, Spanish and German counterparts, alongside New Beat tracks that fit the same mold. The project reached release on 1 September 2023 as “Electronic Bodies – Session 1,” an 88-track EBM charity compilation spanning EBM, New Beat and more contemporary offshoots, with all donations going to psychological support for Ukrainian soldiers and citizens affected by PTSD. Bernard Van Isacker, Side-Line’s chief editor, compiled the release and discussed the project in more detail with Side-Line ahead of its release. “Electronic Bodies 2” is the second volume in that series, with submissions open now.

items.title: Horror Vacui – Shadows Sanctuary (Digital/CD/Vinyl Album – Artoffact Records)
items.summary: The Italian band Horror Vacui has been active since 2010. For their fifth album, they...
items.fullText:
The Italian band Horror Vacui has been active since 2010. For their fifth album, they have teamed up with Artoffact Records, a move that will undoubtedly help them reach a wider audience. “Shadows Sanctuary” explores darkness as a sanctuary in a world increasingly dominated by exposure, visibility, and instability. Through themes such as identity, isolation, love, and grief, the album reclaims darkness as a space for authenticity, protection, and quiet resistance.

The album consists of 10 tracks that immediately draw us back into the band’s dark musical universe. Straddling the line between Dark-Wave and Post-Punk, Horror Vacui delivers a powerful production driven by dynamic drumming. The quintessential 80s-style guitar work cuts through with intensity, evoking the brooding, doom-laden atmosphere typically associated with the genre. The singer’s deep vocal timbre adds a haunting quality, as if guiding the listener through a funeral ceremony.

While I have never associated Horror Vacui with innovation, they certainly know how to capture the spirit and soul of the 80s. In my view, the album lacks a genuine climax, but it will undoubtedly resonate with fans of the genre. (Rating:7).

Listen to “Writing On The Wall”:

About Horror Vacui

Horror Vacui formed in Bologna, Italy in 2010 and have worked through changing line-ups ever since. The band built a catalogue of four albums and numerous singles on guitar-driven songs that fuse deathrock and post-punk, and toured worldwide behind them. Their second album “Return Of The Empire” was first issued on CD by Horror Pain Gore Death at the end of 2014 and later on vinyl by Avant! Records. After their fourth album in 2020 the group went quiet for several years, returning in 2024 with a limited two-track 7″ single.

That return also brought a line-up change, with former guitar player Marzia moving to the drum stool. The 2024 single served as the prelude to “Shadows Sanctuary”, released on 7 August 2026 on limited green vinyl LP, CD and digitally as the band’s first album in six years and their debut for Artoffact Records.

items.title: Corlyx and Mark Gemini Thwaite release new single ‘Die Young’
items.summary: Corlyx releases new single "Die Young" featuring Mark Gemini Thwaite via Out Of Line Music, introducing the album "The Crimson Tapes," due 19 March 2027.
items.fullText:
Gothic rock act Corlyx has released a new single, “Die Young,” featuring guitarist Mark Gemini Thwaite of The Mission, Tricky and Peter Murphy, out now via Out Of Line Music with an official video directed by singer Caitlin Stokes.

Corlyx formed in Los Angeles and now operates between the UK and Turin, built around Stokes on vocals, guitarist and producer Brandon Ashley, bassist Davide Rocco and drummer Flow Toulman. On “Die Young,” Stokes sings about machines, manufactured disease and a generation frightened by a collapsing future, while Thwaite layers flamenco-style acoustic guitar, inspired by John McGeoch, against the band’s electric rhythms.

Thwaite recalls how the collaboration came together: “When Caitlin invited me to record some guitar ideas…in its demo stage, I was struck by the energy of the song and its post-punk atmosphere. Looking forward to hearing it on the dancefloor!”

“Die Young” introduces The Crimson Tapes, Corlyx’s forthcoming thirteen-track album, due 19 March 2027 through Out Of Line Music. It follows 2025’s “Purple Pain.”

“Die Young” is available to stream now via Out Of Line Music.

About Corlyx

The band works across gothic rock, dark wave and death pop, with Stokes writing and directing much of its visual side alongside Ashley’s production. Corlyx’s catalogue includes the singles “Kill Cave” featuring Suzi Sabotage, “Wasted And Alone,” “Zombie Kid” and the 2025 album “Purple Pain,” released through Out Of Line Music. “Die Young,” released in 2026, introduces the follow-up album, The Crimson Tapes, due 19 March 2027.

Thwaite, who guests on guitar for “Die Young,” is an English musician born in Birmingham in 1965 who has recorded and toured with UK gothic rock band The Mission across multiple studio albums, served as touring and recording guitarist for trip hop artist Tricky, and worked extensively with Bauhaus vocalist Peter Murphy. He also recorded with Primitive Race and PIG on Metropolis Records, released solo material as MGT, and in 2025 formed the post-punk band Sevendials with Chris Connelly and Paul Ferguson of Killing Joke.

items.title: John X Belmonte releases single ‘A Sky Full of Black Stars’
items.summary: John X Belmonte releases the darkwave single "A Sky Full of Black Stars" and its video, out 12 November 2026 on Bandcamp.
items.fullText:
New York City darkwave artist John X Belmonte has released a new single, “A Sky Full of Black Stars,” on Bandcamp on 12 November 2026, alongside an official video.

The track opens on hushed, howling textures over a synth bassline before church bells and a breakdown lead into a deep, gospel-inflected vocal rise. Belmonte’s lyrics turn on the idea that two people can share a world while perceiving it in entirely different ways.

The video sets Belmonte’s black-clad cast in a candlelit bar, intercut with bare branches, faceted black stars and a procession of dark cars moving through the city at night.

Belmonte sums up the song’s title plainly, admitting: “What does it mean? I’m not totally sure myself. Something like: where some people see darkness, a void, nothing at all – others (like me) see a sky full of black stars.”

“A Sky Full of Black Stars” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp.

About John X Belmonte

John X Belmonte is an independent dark wave, goth and synth goth artist based in New York City. His catalogue of singles includes “Visitation,” “Her Curse,” “Beautiful Night,” “Cassandra,” “My Kind,” “Before My Eyes,” “Monomania,” “He Visits Her Grave” and “Golden Lore,” alongside the demo album “Turn On The Darklight.”

“A Sky Full of Black Stars,” released 12 November 2026, continues Belmonte’s run of singles exploring mortality, dreams and romantic longing against a backdrop of synth-driven dark wave.

items.title: Deathday returns with new single ‘Hungry Ghosts’
items.summary: Deathday releases new single "Hungry Ghosts" on Bandcamp, 13 November 2026, the first taste of upcoming album "Sans Soleil."
items.fullText:
Los Angeles dark wave duo Deathday has released its first new single in more than a decade, “Hungry Ghosts,” out on Bandcamp on 13 November 2026. The track is the first preview of an upcoming album, “Sans Soleil.”

Deathday, the project of brothers Alex and Giovanni Guillén, recorded “Hungry Ghosts” with producer Matia Simovich at Infinite Power Studios in Los Angeles, with additional recording at The Doppelgänger. Giovanni Guillén sings and plays guitar and bass VI on the track; Alex Guillén handles production, recording and programming alongside Simovich, who also mixed it. Josh Bonati mastered the single.

The track grew out of a reversed instrumental loop that became its backbone, an approach the band ties to surrealist touchstones such as Jean Cocteau, Ingmar Bergman and David Lynch. Giovanni Guillén explains: “We write a lot from the unconscious, surrealist perspective of a person, place, or atmosphere. Characters that aren’t all there. Realities that shift and turn.”

“Hungry Ghosts” is available as a digital single on Bandcamp and via streaming services.

About Deathday

Deathday, formerly known as Deathday Party, is a Los Angeles post-punk and dark wave band formed in Santa Ana, California, in 2008 by brothers Alex and Giovanni Guillén. The pair made their live debut at The Smell in Los Angeles that September, performing as a duo with a drum machine before later expanding to a trio.

The band’s self-titled debut album, “Deathday,” followed in March 2012 on Sweating Tapes and the French label Desire, after the French label had asked the group to expand an earlier self-released EP, “Ghost Pains” (2010), into a full-length. A split EP with Bestial Mouths and the “No Future” EP, both also on Sweating Tapes and Desire, followed in 2013.

Deathday went on hiatus after that run of releases, with Alex Guillén working primarily as a DJ, producer and film composer. “Hungry Ghosts,” released 13 November 2026, marks the band’s return and the first single from the forthcoming album “Sans Soleil.”

items.title: Boustrophedon releases debut album ‘pathOS’
items.summary: Boustrophedon releases debut album "pathOS" on Bandcamp, 13 November 2026, mixing industrial, EBM and post-punk from Los Angeles.
items.fullText:
Los Angeles industrial project Boustrophedon has released its debut full-length album, “pathOS,” on Bandcamp on 13 November 2026. The ten-track record leans into EBM and industrial, pulling the project’s machinery toward the muscular electronic sound of acts like DAF and Front 242.

Boustrophedon is the solo project of a musician going by Alex, who conceived it in Syracuse, New York before relocating to Los Angeles. The move pushed the project’s sound away from its earlier gothic rock inclinations and toward the heavier electronic body music heard on “pathOS.”

The album’s ten tracks are “SIM.biont,” “Cold Steel,” “BDPF,” “–git-purged,” “Circuits Keep Historical Precipitates,” “Bathic Zone,” “L1mb0” featuring Æon Presley, “A Moratorium,” “Cult.Tech.” and “4RR34R5.” Across the record, Alex takes aim at social media, online dating and artificial intelligence as everyday sources of alienation.

On the track “SIM.biont,” Alex turns that same scrutiny on the underground scene itself, saying: “SIM.biont is a bit of us taking the piss out of ourselves. We see stagnation and saturation in much of the underground/dark scenes that have risen up, but we’re trying not to add to the heap. Key word, trying.”

“pathOS” is available as a digital album on Bandcamp.

About Boustrophedon

Before the move to Los Angeles, Boustrophedon leaned closer to gothic rock and post-punk; the relocation brought a harder, EBM-indebted electronic sound to the foreground. The project built up to its debut full-length through a run of EPs and singles on Bandcamp, including “Syndrome X,” “The Colossus,” “Raison D’etre / Cold Steel,” the remix collection “WINTER // STEEL” and the “SIM.biont” demo, followed by the standalone single “L1mb0” featuring Æon Presley.

“pathOS,” released 13 November 2026, gathers that material’s themes of alienation and surveillance into the project’s first full-length statement.

items.title: Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? revisit ‘En Ordre’ with four mixes and launch new official website
items.summary: Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? release the digital single "En Ordre" in four mixes on November 14, 2026, and launch a new official website in four languages.
items.fullText:
German EBM and electro-punk act Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? released the digital single “En Ordre” on November 14, 2026. The release reworks a track from the band’s 1993 debut album “Tumulte” into four new versions, and coincides with the launch of a new official website.

The band reconstructed the track in four directions instead of remastering the original recording, keeping its industrial and electronic roots. The digital single includes:

  • Clash Mix – a raw, aggressive industrial interpretation.
  • Slow Down Mix – a slower, darker and heavier version.
  • Orchestrale Mix – an arrangement combining orchestral textures with electronic elements.
  • The Flood (Riot Mix) – an alternative version of “The Flood,” a new Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? composition.

“The Flood” is also one of two new tracks slated for the band’s vinyl EP “No Bottom – No Top,” due January 15, 2027 on Emmo.biz Records, alongside reworked versions of “Souvenir” and “Ewigkeit.” “En Ordre” connects that upcoming material to the band’s early catalogue. That catalogue is being reissued digitally through the Norwegian label Sub Culture Records. The campaign began November 13, 2026 with the 1994 album “Annorlunda” and the 1995 album “Les Enfants Sauvages.”

Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? launch new official website

Alongside “En Ordre,” Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? launched a new official website at sabotageqcqc.online, with sections covering releases, the band’s back catalogue, archives, news and band information. The site is available in English, German, French and Spanish.

About Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.?

Sabotage Q.C.Q.C.? is a German EBM and electro-punk act whose current lineup includes Isabelle Gernand, Marc Werner, Detlef Weinreich and Johannes Buchner. The band’s recorded history goes back more than three decades, starting with the 1993 album “Tumulte,” followed by “Annorlunda” (1994) and “Les Enfants Sauvages” (1995).

Those three 1990s albums are now being reissued digitally through Sub Culture Records, a label run by longtime band associate Per Aksel Lundgreen. The campaign opened November 13, 2026 with “Annorlunda” and “Les Enfants Sauvages,” with “Tumulte”-era material to follow. The band is also preparing new material through Germany’s Emmo.biz Records: a limited 12-inch vinyl EP, “No Bottom – No Top,” is scheduled for January 15, 2027, carrying the new tracks “The Flood” and “Impuls Kontakt” alongside reworked versions of “Souvenir” and “Ewigkeit,” ahead of a full-length studio album planned for later in 2027.

“En Ordre,” released digitally on November 14, 2026, sits between those two strands of activity. It revisits “Tumulte”-era material in four new mixes and previews “The Flood” in an alternate version. The band’s new official website gathers its reissue campaign, new material and archive in one place.

items.title: Marcel Miska shares gothic darkwave single ‘Happy New Year (Farewell My Dear)’
items.summary: Actor and voiceover artist Marcel Miska released the gothic synth-pop single "Happy New Year (Farewell My Dear)" on November 9, 2026, on Spotify.
items.fullText:
London-based actor, author and voiceover artist Marcel Miska released the gothic darkwave and synth-pop single “Happy New Year (Farewell My Dear)” on November 9, 2026, streaming on Spotify. Miska wrote and composed the track himself.

Miska built the song’s narrative around the Spectre of Newby Church, a 1963 photograph taken inside the Church of Christ the Consoler in North Yorkshire and long cited as one of Britain’s best-known ghost images. Miska described the track’s story: “That eerie atmosphere sparked a fictional narrative set on New Year’s Eve in 1803, telling the dark story of a murder whose victim and perpetrator have been locked in an eternal, supernatural battle in the afterlife, forced to settle their scores time and time again.” Musically, Miska stated, the track blends cold synth-pop textures with the song’s gothic and darkwave themes.

About Marcel Miska

Marcel Miska is a London-based actor, author and voiceover artist, represented through Spotlight and credited on IMDb. “Happy New Year (Farewell My Dear)” is his new single, released independently on November 9, 2026, and streaming on Spotify. Miska wrote, composed and performed the track, drawing its narrative from the Spectre of Newby Church ghost photograph and setting it against a backdrop of cold synth-pop production.

items.title: Diskodiktator remixes Peter Sjöholm’s ‘Videon Blinkar Noll’

Swedish synthpop artist Peter Sjöholm released the single “Videon Blinkar Noll (Diskodiktator Remix)” on 5 November 2026 through his own label Computer Killed The Recordstore. The remix continues an exchange between Sjöholm and Swedish synth duo Diskodiktator that began the previous month.

In October 2026, Diskodiktator released “Bättre Tider (Peter Sjöholm Remix)”, a Sjöholm rework of the opening track from their album “Det Trötta Hatets Stad”. Sjöholm’s “Videon Blinkar Noll”, originally released in May 2026, now returns the favor with a Diskodiktator remix. Further remixes of “Videon Blinkar Noll” are planned through the autumn and winter, with contributions announced from Goto80, Futuro and Compute.

“Videon Blinkar Noll (Diskodiktator Remix)” is available on Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, Amazon Music and Tidal.

About Peter Sjöholm

Peter Sjöholm has written and released Swedish-language synthpop for over two decades. His recent singles include “Tankar Vid Ett Piano” (2024), “Livets Återkomst” (2025) and “Videon Blinkar Noll” (2026), the latter now the subject of the Diskodiktator remix series. items.title: Eden Synthetic Corps – Away From Human Standards (Digital/CD Album – Scanner / Dark Dimensions)
items.summary: The Portuguese band Eden Synthetic Corps (ESC) is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year. It...
items.fullText:
The Portuguese band Eden Synthetic Corps (ESC) is celebrating its 20th anniversary this year. It has been two decades since the release of their debut album, “Matte”—a record I vividly remember making a real impact on the scene. Since then, the band has continued its journey, releasing a total of seven albums. Over the years, lineup changes happened, and the band’s sound has evolved from a distinctly Dark-Electro style towards a more Industrial approach, with guitars playing an increasingly prominent role. Now a five-piece outfit, the band uses this latest release to look back on its career. Although I wouldn’t describe it as a traditional ‘best-of’ compilation, the album features two tracks selected from each of their previous albums, reworked to reflect the band’s current style and creative vision.

The result is a collection of 14 tracks in which the original Dark-Electro roots remain clearly audible. The sound is dark, aggressive and, at times, raw, driven by searing lead synths and dynamic rhythms. The guitars gradually take on a more prominent role, adding an Industrial edge to the overall sound. There is an excellent balance between the electronic structures and the power of the guitars and bass. What we (re)discover here is an overwhelming sound, complemented by intense, hard-hitting vocals. The tracks have been carefully selected and, even better, meticulously reworked, resulting in a consistently strong collection of songs.

I have always felt that ESC never received the recognition they truly deserved. As far as I’m concerned, this album only serves to confirm their immense talent. (Rating:8½).

Listen to “Northern Hunter – Rework 2026”:

About Eden Synthetic Corps

Eden Synthetic Corps formed in 2005 in Portugal and issued its debut album “Matte” on Dark Dimensions in 2006, followed by “Enhancer” in 2008 and “Eight Thousand Square Feet” in 2010. “Breathing Salt” in 2013 opened a more experimental period, and Side-Line reviewed “Sandwalkers” in November 2015 as the album that pushed the sound toward a more organic feel. “Gold” followed in 2019, and the band contributed to the label retrospective “A Human Scan(ner) – The 20th Anniversary Compilation” in 2021. The seventh album, “The Encyclopaedia Of Black“, arrived in 2022 with a turn toward industrial and crossover sounds and a changed line-up. Founder João Vairinhos remains the band’s creative core, alongside Marco P. on vocals, Walter T. on bass, Daniel R. on drums and Ricardo R. on guitars. “Away From Human Standards” revisits two tracks from each of those seven albums in this current line-up.

items.title: Gamma Vortex – Painfather (Digital/CD Album – Scanner / Dark Dimensions)
items.summary: Martin Rudefelt is a Swedish artist best known for his involvement with the band Cryo....
items.fullText:
Martin Rudefelt is a Swedish artist best known for his involvement with the band Cryo. With Gamma Vortex, however, he has taken a different direction in recent years, leaning more towards the Dark-Electro genre. His debut EPs, “Undertaker” and “Hatefeeder,” hit me like a bombshell. This first official album brings together the eight original tracks from those EPs, supplemented by four brand-new songs -including two alternative mixes.

The original tracks from both EPs remain as impressive as ever, while the four new additions pack an extra punch. Gamma Vortex often walks a fine line between Dark-Electro and EBM, but what consistently blows me away is the production. Every track is meticulously crafted down to the finest detail, boasting a polished, high-end sound. Martin’s haunting vocals fit perfectly into the overall aesthetic, contributing significantly to the atmosphere he creates. Expect incredible basslines combined with powerful string arrangements that add depth and weight, all layered with an impressive arsenal of vintage synth sounds. Gamma Vortex represents intelligent music, steering clear of cheap clichés. This is a project with a distinct sonic DNA, a quality that shines through once again in the new, additional, tracks, which are yet another highlight. They create a menacing atmosphere and offer clever nods to EBM, while also including a more subdued piece whose power derives primarily from its textures.

“Painfather” is a true masterpiece from a project whose name you won’t soon forget. This is Dark-Electro of the highest calibre, crafted by a genuine genius. Given what Rudefelt has already demonstrated with Cryo, however, that should come as no surprise. (Rating:9½).

Listen to “Staring At The Wall – Concrete Mix”:

About Gamma Vortex

Gamma Vortex is the solo Dark-Electro project of Swedish musician Martin Rudefelt, who is also known for his work in Cryo. Side-Line reviewed Cryo’s “The Fall Of Man” in 2019, the same year the band gave Side-Line a Click Interview. Rudefelt released the Gamma Vortex EPs “Undertaker” and “Hatefeeder” as digital reissues on Scanner’s Dark Dimensions imprint, with “Undertaker” following an earlier 2024 edition on Dungeon Production. “Painfather” gathers the eight tracks from both EPs with four new songs, including two alternative mixes.

items.title: CTRL CLICK Confronts the Machinery of Mortality in “Angel of Death” — Debut Album “Systems for Disassembly” Out Now!
items.summary: Patient as gravity Final as dust The most unsettling figure in the hospital corridor may be the one who speaks softly, knows the procedure, and never needs to hurry. Under… The post CTRL CLICK Confronts the Machinery of Mortality in “Angel of Death” — Debut Al
items.fullText:
Patient as gravity
Final as dust 

The most unsettling figure in the hospital corridor may be the one who speaks softly, knows the procedure, and never needs to hurry. Under fluorescent light, death acquires a bedside manner, moving between the ventilator and the waiting room with the patience of someone whose appointment book always fills. The body becomes a collection of readings, while the person inside it waits for someone to look up from the screen.

CTRL CLICK, the industrial project of Rockford, Illinois artist Eric Nofsinger, enters that corridor on Angel of Death, the opening track from debut album Systems for Disassembly. Released November 6 through Negative Gain Productions, the fourteen-song record examines the machinery surrounding contemporary life: the workplace, the pharmacy, the digital feed, and the institutions entrusted with keeping us alive.

Angel of Death begins amid dirgeful mechanical drones, metallic clanks, and muffled radio chatter. A spoken repetition of the title circles through the opening before a machine-driven snare establishes its heavy, deliberate tread. Nofsinger’s growl grinds against the beat as uneasy electronic textures spread through the gaps. There is a factory-floor physicality to the arrangement, its accumulated noise suggesting machinery running somewhere beyond the walls. Fans of Ministry, Skinny Puppy, Front Line Assembly, and Front 242 will recognize the appetite for sampling, oppressive atmosphere, and percussion that makes the whole room feel operational.

The lyrics give the title figure an unnervingly practical presence. Death works through sterile contact and quiet procedure; religious spectacle falls away as Nofsinger contemplates the finality of the body. Yet tenderness complicates the dread. His words reach toward the possibility of mercy, asking whether the passage out of life might offer companionship to someone already frightened and alone. That uncertainty gives the song its emotional pressure: the person approaching the bed could bring relief, oblivion, or both.

The accompanying video carries those ideas through a succession of nearly monochrome hospital rooms, deserted corridors, and ruined interiors. A white-winged figure occupies the darkness while an ECG trace cuts across the frame. Hands press against frosted glass; surgical instruments, an IV bag, and an empty bed turn familiar objects of care into sources of unease. Large white and turquoise lyrics tilt, advance, and break across the images, making the words feel as physically intrusive as the percussion. The contrast between soft feathers and hard clinical surfaces keeps the angel’s intentions troublingly open.

Watch the video for Angel of Death below:

Across Systems for Disassembly, that clinical setting opens onto a broader landscape of employment, addiction, surveillance, and corporate control. Hospital wards and server farms belong to the same world, connected by the habit of translating people into figures. Each song approaches a different point where a human need meets an administrative process, with conformity and mortality feeding into the everyday business of getting through another shift.

Our God locates divinity among cooling towers and compromised passwords, imagining technological authority with an intimate knowledge of its subjects. Good as Dead follows a body kept barely functional while work and rent continue to claim their share. The biometric checkpoint provokes the insubordination of Insolent, while closing track (Kill) the Vampire considers how prolonged proximity to exploitation can teach its victims to become predators themselves. Together, these songs turn the album’s title into a question about responsibility: taking a system apart also means examining the habits it has installed in you.

Nofsinger produced and mixed the album himself, with mastering by Rob Robinson of Kevorkian Death Cycle and ohGr. Systems for Disassembly is out now on CD and digital formats via Negative Gain Productions.

Listen below and order the album here.

Nofsinger brings three decades of experience in video games to this examination of technology and corporate life. Hired in 1994 as High Voltage Software’s first artist, he helped grow the studio to 185 developers and 117 shipped games, with its work including Fortnite, Mortal Kombat X, and Baldur’s Gate: Dark Alliance. He led its creative work through its 2020 sale to Keywords Studios. With CTRL CLICK, the industrial records he grew up on meet a working life spent inside the structures his debut now takes apart.

items.title: “From the Screen to the Grave” — Boustrophedon Confront Digital Alienation and Manufactured Identity on Industrial Synth Debut Album “pathOS”
items.summary: The best you can be is a reflection Keep them staring at shit Served too softcore Then it ain’t worth a lick America has become a magnificent junkyard of obsolete… The post “From the Screen to the Grave” — Boustrophedon Confront Digital Alienation and Manufact
items.fullText:
The best you can be is a reflection

Keep them staring at shit

Served too softcore

Then it ain’t worth a lick

America has become a magnificent junkyard of obsolete promises, where every new technological miracle comes equipped with another way to make you miserable, lonely, and dependent on a machine that wants your money. Your phone knows your sexual preferences, your refrigerator probably has political opinions, and somewhere in California, a billionaire is teaching artificial intelligence to replace the few remaining pleasures of being alive and grounding planes in the process. Welcome to the future, comrades. Please accept the updated terms and conditions.

Into this electronic madhouse comes Boustrophedon, otherwise known as Turn The Ox, with pathOS, a debut full-length that takes several decades of industrial music, post-punk, and electronic body music, feeds them through the American meat grinder, and asks whether anyone remembers how to have a good time while civilization loses its marbles.

Originally conceived in Syracuse, New York, the project has undergone a considerable mutation since Alex relocated to Los Angeles, trading some of its earlier gothic rock inclinations for the muscular electronic machinery of DAF, Front 242, Depeche Mode, Chromeo, and early Sextile. The results suggest a collision between a German industrial nightclub, a Rust Belt factory undergoing demolition, and a particularly deranged episode of The Twilight Zone.

And what a splendid collection of contemporary diseases they’ve assembled! Social media, online dating, artificial intelligence, and the creeping suspicion that your personality has become a secondhand reproduction of somebody else’s secondhand reproduction all receive their turn beneath the examination lamp. The record’s title, pathOS, provides a wonderfully nasty little pun, suggesting an operating system infected with the miserable business of existence.

On SIM.biont, the band turns its attention toward the underground itself, where fashionable misery has become practically a cottage industry.

“SIM.biont is a bit of us taking the piss out of ourselves,” says Alex. “We see stagnation and saturation in much of the underground/dark scenes that have risen up, but we’re trying not to add to the heap. Key word, trying.”

Their self-awareness gives the enterprise its necessary dose of mischief. After all, how many people can dress themselves in black, operate a synthesizer, and deliver another lecture about alienation before somebody starts selling alienation as a subscription service?

Even the accompanying photography participates in this argument. Retro-futuristic snowsuits planted against the enormous emptiness of California’s Big Bear and Kelso Dunes suggest astronauts stranded on a planet already conquered by its own inventions. Analogue film meets digital imagery, technology confronts wilderness, and American transcendentalism gets dragged into the twenty-first century wearing protective clothing.

pathOS leaves us with a wonderfully uneasy question: How do you take part in a civilization whose operating instructions you’re desperate to rewrite? Boustrophedon’s answer: turn up the analogue machines, dance in the meantime, and figure it all out as you go.

items.title: vidnaObmana’s ‘The River Of Appearance’ turns 30
items.summary: Projekt Records marked 30 years of vidnaObmana's ambient album 'The River Of Appearance' with a new Dirk Serries interview on Opus Zine.
items.fullText:
Projekt Records marked the 30th anniversary of vidnaObmana’s ambient album “The River Of Appearance”, originally released in 1996, with a new interview in which Opus Zine’s Jason Morehead spoke to Belgian composer Dirk Serries about the album’s recording, its 2006 rework by Oregon ensemble Dreams In Exile, and its Zoharum 25th-anniversary edition. The interview, “30 Years of Serenity: Dirk Serries Reflects on vidnaObmana’s The River of Appearance”, is available on Opus Zine.

“The River Of Appearance” consists of eight pieces built around sparse piano lines, drifting keyboard loops and organic rainstick sounds. Alternative Press critic Bryan Reesman described it at the time as music in which “sparse, pretty piano lines float over shimmering walls of electronics, evoking a melancholic yet romantic feeling,” with “cyclical melodies” interweaving “in a slowly moving stream of sound.”

“The River Of Appearance” is available as a name-your-price digital album, and as a 10th-anniversary 2CD edition (which adds a disc of the album reinterpreted on traditional instruments by Dreams In Exile) for $15, both on Bandcamp.

About vidnaObmana

vidnaObmana was the primary recording name of Belgian composer Dirk Serries, used across a body of ambient and dark ambient work that included “The River Of Appearance” in 1996. Projekt Records released a 10th-anniversary edition of the album in 2006, pairing the original with a reinterpretation by Oregon ensemble Dreams In Exile performed on traditional instruments; a 25th-anniversary edition followed on the Polish label Zoharum.

Side-Line has previously covered Serries’ work on the 1992 vidnaObmana album “Terrace of Memories”, remastered in collaboration with Projekt founder Sam Rosenthal, including the Kickstarter campaign that funded its physical formats.

Thirty years on, “The River Of Appearance” remains part of Projekt’s active catalogue, with the new Opus Zine interview placing the album’s recording and its various reissues in Serries’ own words.

items.title: Phil Stiles announces double EP ‘I’m Fading’
items.summary: Final Coil frontman Phil Stiles announced the double EP 'I'm Fading', out 11 December 2026 on Nyctophobic Records, with a video premiered on 13 November.
items.fullText:
Final Coil frontman and songwriter Phil Stiles announced a new double EP, “I’m Fading”, set for release on 11 December 2026 via Nyctophobic Records. It is his first original solo material since 2021; this year’s “Plaid and Lead” was a reworking of Matt Steady’s “Velvet and Gold” album rather than new original material.

The title track and first single was released alongside its video on 13 November 2026, viewable on YouTube.

The first disc, the four-track “I’m Fading EP”, features three new tracks recorded with Chris Barber (Crazy Town) on drums, plus a remix of the title track by Seattle-based producer Shane Aungst. The second disc, “Thornhill’s Night Out EP”, is built around electronica, moving from influences including The Orb, Leftfield, Orbital and The Chemical Brothers toward the more abstract sound of Aphex Twin, and closes with a Shane Aungst remix of The Anchorhold’s “Dance Fucker”.

“I’m Fading” will be released as a limited-edition double CD featuring artwork and photography by Final Coil’s Jola Stiles, alongside standalone digital releases on Phil Stiles’ Bandcamp page.

Disc 1, “I’m Fading EP”: “I’m Fading”; “Uprooted”; “Filtered”; “I’m Fading” (Shane Aungst Remix).

Disc 2, “Thornhill’s Night Out EP”: “Dead of the Night”; “Bliss”; “Wiped Out”; “Chemikalized”; “Keep Your Head Down”; “The Walls Gleam in the Darkness”; “Lost in the Aether”; “Dance Fucker” (Shane Aungst Remix).

About Phil Stiles

Phil Stiles is the frontman and songwriter of Final Coil, a project previously covered by Side-Line, including Shane Aungst’s 2022 remix album “The Anchorhold Dissolution”, based on Stiles’ own studio material.

Earlier in 2026, Stiles released “Plaid and Lead”, a reworking of Matt Steady’s “Velvet and Gold” album. “I’m Fading” marks his return to original solo songwriting, drawing on the harder-edged alternative and progressive sound of Final Coil alongside the more electronic, post-punk-leaning material that makes up the second disc.

items.title: Kim Lunner releases new single ‘I Know’
items.summary: Norwegian electronic artist Kim Lunner released the single 'I Know' on Town And Towers Records on 13 November 2026, addressing childhood insecurity.
items.fullText:
Norwegian electronic music producer Kim Lunner released the single “I Know” on 13 November 2026 through Town And Towers Records. The song addresses the contrast between childhood dreams of a secure life and a reality in which, for some children, that security remains out of reach.

Lunner describes the track in his own words: “‘I Know’ is a song about children who dream of something new – freedom, love, and security. But the truth is that it is only a dream. They live in a society where a sense of insecurity is only growing. Stepping out of the shadows and having a home of their own, with a family, remains nothing more than a dream.”

“I Know” is available to stream and buy on Bandcamp, and on major streaming services via orcd.co/iknow__.

About Kim Lunner

Kim Lunner is a Norwegian music producer who has been making music since 2011. He released his first album on 20 May 2020 through Scent Air Records, and began singing on his own recordings that same year. Following the label change prompted by the war in Ukraine, Lunner signed in 2022 with the Danish label Town And Towers Records.

Originally a drummer, Lunner produces his own drum parts and favours slower tempos built around synthesizer patterns, blending synthpop, futurepop and electro with darker electronic textures. His catalogue now runs to more than 25 singles, four EPs and five albums.

In 2023, Lunner joined the Norwegian futurepop band Supercraft, and co-founded the electronic project State of Anguish with fellow Norwegian synth artist Egil Thoms Hansen. Side-Line previously covered Lunner’s 2025 single “With You” and Supercraft’s 2024 reissue of “Select & Operate”.

“I Know” follows that run of releases as Lunner’s latest single under his own name on Town And Towers Records.

items.title: Vlimmer releases new album ‘Kiemenatmung’
items.summary: Berlin darkgaze project Vlimmer released the twelve-track album 'Kiemenatmung' on Blackjack Illuminist Records on 13 November 2026, its sixth full-length.
items.fullText:
Berlin-based darkgaze project Vlimmer released its sixth full-length album, “Kiemenatmung”, on 13 November 2026 via Blackjack Illuminist Records. The twelve-track album is the work of Berlin musician Alexander Leonard Donat, who also runs the label.

The title translates as “gill breathing”, the way fish extract oxygen from water, used on the album as a metaphor for rising deadlines, shifting relationships and mounting anxiety. Donat describes the record as resilience shown through endurance, not triumph, with water imagery of diving under, resurfacing and swimming against invisible currents running through all twelve songs.

Musically, “Kiemenatmung” continues Vlimmer’s blend of post-punk and darkwave, folding in shoegaze guitar textures. According to the label, tracks including “Atemdauer”, “Lockenkopf” and “Besitzergreifung” lean toward techno, while “Augendrang” and “Wasserstand” move into melancholic wave-pop. The album closes with “Lavalunge”, in which the record’s water imagery gives way to fire.

“Kiemenatmung” is available as a name-your-price digital album on Bandcamp.

About Vlimmer

Alexander Leonard Donat founded Blackjack Illuminist Records in Berlin and has released Vlimmer’s music through it ever since, across singles, EPs and now six full-length albums under a self-described “darkgaze” label spanning post-punk and darkwave, with shoegaze and industrial textures layered in.

Side-Line has tracked Vlimmer’s output across several releases, including the 2021 Nirvana cover compilation “Nevermind Reworks”, the 2022 two-track single “Noposition/1979”, the 2023 album “Zerschöpfung”, and, most recently, “Augendrang”, released in October 2026 as the final single ahead of “Kiemenatmung”.

With “Kiemenatmung” now out in full, that single’s b-side cover of The Bangles’ “Eternal Flame” and the “Augendrang” single both take their place within the complete twelve-track album.

items.title: Agent Side Grinder release single ‘The Choir’ on Metropolis Records
items.summary: Agent Side Grinder released 'The Choir' on Metropolis Records on 13 November 2026, their first new single since 2023 and a signing to the US label.
items.fullText:
Swedish electronic post-punk trio Agent Side Grinder released the single “The Choir” on 13 November 2026 via Metropolis Records. It is the band’s first new original single since “Jack Vegas” (2023) and their first release on the American label following their signing to it.

“The Choir” was produced by Jimmy Monell, who has also worked with Kite and Emmon, and was recorded at Agent Side Grinder’s own studio in northwestern Stockholm. The track addresses the power of words and how quickly they can spread, multiply and take on a life of their own.

Agent Side Grinder have also announced a new EP for March 2027, which the band say will eventually form part of a double EP release.

European tour with Then Comes Silence in January 2027

Agent Side Grinder will join fellow Swedish band and Metropolis Records labelmates Then Comes Silence for eight co-headlining European dates in January 2027, with further live activity planned for spring 2027.

Tour dates:

  • 8 January 2027 – Hamburg, Molotow (Germany)
  • 9 January 2027 – Detmold, Owls N Bats Festival (Germany)
  • 10 January 2027 – Oberhausen, Kulttempel (Germany)
  • 12 January 2027 – Chambéry, Brin de Zinc (France)
  • 13 January 2027 – Liège, Deux Ours (Belgium)
  • 14 January 2027 – Hannover, Lux (Germany)
  • 15 January 2027 – Aarhus, Train (Denmark)
  • 16 January 2027 – Copenhagen, Hotel Cecil (Denmark)

About Agent Side Grinder

Agent Side Grinder formed in Stockholm in the late 2000s, founded by Peter Fristedt and Johan Lange. Vocalist Emanuel Åström joined the band in 2017, after which the group released the albums “A/X” (2019) and “Jack Vegas” (2023), developing a sound built on analogue electronics, driving rhythms and dark melodies within Sweden’s electronic post-punk scene.

Side-Line has previously covered the band’s back catalogue, including the first clear-vinyl pressing of ‘A/X’ in 2024, and Beborn Beton’s use of an Agent Side Grinder remix on their own single in 2025. The band’s influence has also reached younger acts, with groups such as Molchat Doma and Boy Harsher citing Agent Side Grinder as an influence.

“The Choir” is Agent Side Grinder’s first release under the Metropolis Records deal, ahead of the January 2027 tour with Then Comes Silence and the EP due in March 2027.

About Silent Weapon

Oxford-based musician Umair Chaudhry records as Silent Weapon, mixing dark-electro and industrial electronics with elements of noise. The project’s catalogue includes the releases “Eggshells,” “Purge,” “Purged,” “Demonology” and “Demonised,” along with the EP “Cognitive Dissonance.” Its 2023 EP, “The Fear Of The Possibility Of Chaos,” released on Blindsight Records on 10 November 2023, paired three original tracks with a cover of Voivod’s “Angel Rat” and was reviewed by Side-Line, which highlighted the tracks “Menticide” and the EP’s title track. “Oblivion Seeker,” Silent Weapon‘s third album, continues the project’s run of self-released dark-electro material, bringing in Octavia Freud, Black Tish and Deeq as guest vocalists across its eight tracks.

items.title: KÁRYYN reworks Depeche Mode’s ‘Survive’ for ‘Sunrise on the Reaping’ soundtrack
items.summary: Depeche Mode's "Survive" gets an Arena Mix reworked by KÁRYYN for "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" soundtrack, out 13 November 2026 on MCA.
items.fullText:
Depeche Mode‘s “Survive” appears in a new Arena Mix reworked by KÁRYYN on “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (The Album),” released 13 November 2026 on MCA. The track, listed as “Survive (Arena Mix | KÁRYYN Rework),” is track 19 of the 29-track soundtrack and streams digitally from release day alongside double-CD and purple-vinyl double-LP gatefold editions.

Martin Gore and Dave Gahan wrote “Survive,” and James Ford produced the original version, recorded during the sessions for Depeche Mode’s 2023 studio album “Memento Mori.” The song later appeared as a bonus track on the band’s 2025 live album “Memento Mori: Mexico City,” alongside “Life 2.0,” “Give Yourself To Me” and “In The End.” For the Arena Mix, KÁRYYN reworked the track and added new vocal parts.

“The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping (The Album)” also features Kacey Musgraves, Stevie Nicks, The Smashing Pumpkins, Noah Kahan, Jennifer Lawrence and The Cure, who close the record. The soundtrack ties to the film “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” directed by Francis Lawrence and starring Joseph Zada as a young Haymitch Abernathy, which opens in cinemas on 20 November 2026, a week after the album.

About Depeche Mode

Formed in Basildon, Essex, in 1980, the band’s founding members were Vince Clarke, Martin Gore, Andy Fletcher and Dave Gahan. The band debuted with “Speak & Spell” in 1981, the only Depeche Mode album written primarily by Clarke, who left that year to form Yazoo and later Erasure. Gore became the band’s main songwriter from “A Broken Frame” (1982) onward. Alan Wilder joined in 1982 and remained a member through “Songs of Faith and Devotion” (1993), departing in 1995.

The band’s catalogue includes “Construction Time Again” (1983), “Some Great Reward” (1984), “Black Celebration” (1986), “Music for the Masses” (1987), “Violator” (1990), “Songs of Faith and Devotion” (1993), “Ultra” (1997), “Exciter” (2001), “Playing the Angel” (2005), “Sounds of the Universe” (2009), “Delta Machine” (2013), “Spirit” (2017) and “Memento Mori” (2023), the latter produced by James Ford and the first album made after Andy Fletcher’s death in May 2022. Depeche Mode now continues as the duo of Dave Gahan and Martin Gore, who in October also released a remixed version of “Cross Whisper” under the name MG x CD + JL = with Cliff Damavandi. The band’s three sold-out 2023 concerts at Mexico City’s Foro Sol Stadium on the Memento Mori World Tour were documented on the concert film and live album “Memento Mori: Mexico City,” whose bonus tracks include “Survive,” the song now reworked for the Hunger Games soundtrack.

items.title: New Order’s ‘Movement’ turns 45 on 13 November
items.summary: New Order released their debut album "Movement" through Factory Records on 13 November 1981. The album turns 45 this year.
items.fullText:
English post-punk band New Order released their debut studio album, “Movement,” through Factory Records on 13 November 1981. Martin Hannett produced the record. “Movement” turns 45 this year.

The band recorded “Movement” between 24 April and 4 May 1981 at Strawberry Studios in Stockport, with Chris Nagle engineering and John Leckie and Flood assisting. The sessions followed the end of Joy Division after singer Ian Curtis’s death in May 1980, and “Movement” was the first album the surviving trio of Bernard Sumner, Peter Hook and Stephen Morris made as New Order, now joined by keyboardist Gillian Gilbert. The album reached number 30 on the UK Albums Chart and number one on the UK Independent Albums Chart. No single was taken from the album.

The eight-track record runs 35 minutes and 20 seconds:

  1. “Dreams Never End”
  2. “Truth”
  3. “Senses”
  4. “Chosen Time”
  5. “ICB”
  6. “The Him”
  7. “Doubts Even Here”
  8. “Denial”

Sumner sang lead vocals, guitars, melodica and synthesisers; Hook played bass and sang lead on “Dreams Never End” and “Doubts Even Here”; Gilbert played synthesisers and guitars and spoke the words on “Doubts Even Here”; Morris played drums and synthesisers. Hook later described the record’s production as unsettled: “I actually liked Movement, but I know why nobody else likes it.” “Movement” streams on Spotify.

About New Order

New Order formed in Manchester in 1980, after Joy Division ended with Ian Curtis’s death. Surviving members Bernard Sumner, Peter Hook and Stephen Morris continued as a trio and were joined that October by keyboardist Gillian Gilbert. The new band’s debut single, “Ceremony,” a song written in Joy Division’s final weeks, appeared on Factory Records in January 1981. “Movement” followed that November, produced by Martin Hannett, who had also produced Joy Division’s two studio albums. The record marked the band’s transition from Curtis’s former group toward their own identity, mixing post-punk guitar work with the synthesisers and sequencers that would come to define their sound.

New Order’s next album, “Power, Corruption & Lies” (1983), pushed further into electronics, and its non-album single “Blue Monday” became the best-selling 12-inch single in UK chart history. “Low-Life” (1985) and “Brotherhood” (1986) continued to split guitar-driven and electronic material across their tracklists, and “Technique” (1989) and “Republic” (1993) carried the band through the end of Factory Records. Forty-five years after it introduced the group, “Movement” remains the first chapter of New Order’s catalogue.
